install_description: Install OpenConnect for Mac with one command. Open a teammate’s profile, enter your username and connect.
disclaimer: Independent project, not an official OpenConnect product. Not affiliated with OpenConnect or Cisco. AnyConnect describes protocol compatibility.
title: OpenConnect for Mac — work VPN on your Mac
description: Work VPN on your Mac: SSO sign-in, selected networks and corporate DNS, and recovery after sleep. An open-source client built on OpenConnect.
lead: SSO, the networks you need, and recovery after sleep. A native macOS menu, open source, built on OpenConnect.
demo_alt: OpenConnect for Mac menu: connect, switch off a network, pause
demo_caption: The real menu on a demo profile.
p1_t: SSO: fill in multiple sign-in steps
p1_d: Teach the web form once. Passwords and one-time codes come from Keychain, KeePassXC or your own command. Cisco single-sign-on-v2 uses a WebKit sign-in window.
p2_t: Work networks through VPN; everything else uses your usual connection
p2_d: Only the networks in your profile go through the tunnel; everything else, home network included, goes the usual way. Switch them from the menu without reconnecting.
p3_t: Smart DNS: yours and the company’s at once
p3_d: Company domains resolve through the company DNS, everything else through yours. Switch individual zones from the menu. System DNS stays untouched.
p4_t: A native macOS menu with pause
p4_d: Built with SwiftUI. Pause removes the app’s routes and DNS zones while keeping the VPN session; resume restores them. Profiles and logs open from the menu.
p5_d: The supervisor brings the connection back after sleep, Wi-Fi changes and dropped links, without opening a sign-in window on its own.
install_note: This command downloads the installer from GitHub. It offers to install missing Apple tools and Homebrew, installs OpenConnect for Mac and opens the app. The system helper needs your Mac administrator password.
requirements: macOS 14.4+ · access to an AnyConnect-compatible gateway
profile_link: I have a configured profile from a teammate
compat_live: Real connection: an AnyConnect-compatible gateway with Keycloak, macOS 26 on Apple Silicon. Used daily by the author.
compat_ci: Automated checks: ocserv and test SSO gateways. These do not confirm compatibility with real Okta or Microsoft Entra ID deployments.
compat_limits: Requires macOS 14.4+. Intel and macOS 14.4–15 have no real-device verification. A clean installation and first sign-in on another Mac have not been tested yet.
feedback_link: Tried your gateway? Tell us how it went
feedback_note: A short report helps clarify compatibility. No company name, gateway address or sign-in details needed.
